bidId.description: Link an existing bid to this project (both sides), or `null` to unlink. Requires the `bids:write` scope too. Refused with 409 when the bid already belongs to another live project or this project already has a different bid — unlink first. kind.description: item = priced line; section = header grouping the rows after it; note = customer-visible text.

isOptional.description: An optional (alternate) priced line, quoted outside the bid total.

markName.description: Human-friendly mark name, e.g. W-01. Null on section and note rows.

quantity.description: Quantity. Sections and notes are not priced.

unitPrice.description: Pre-markup direct cost per unit (before margin, overhead, commission, and distributed project costs). Not the customer price — use customerUnitPrice.

total.description: Pre-markup line cost. Summing these does not equal the bid subtotal. Use customerTotal.

customerUnitPrice.description: Customer-facing unit price after markup and this line's share of distributed costs. Null on section and note rows. An optional line is priced on its own and is excluded from the bid subtotal.

customerTotal.description: Customer-facing line total in dollars, reconciled to the cent. Null on section and note rows. The sum over priced, non-optional lines equals the bid's pre-discount subtotal.

sellTaxPercent.description: Per-line sales-tax rate (0–100). Null inherits the bid's tax rate; 0 exempts the line.

buyTaxPercent.description: Per-line purchase-tax rate (0–100) on a flat line's cost. Null inherits the product's rate.

order.description: Sort position within the bid. A section covers every following row until the next section.

lineItems.description: Present on GET /bids/{id}. unitPrice and total are pre-markup cost; customerUnitPrice and customerTotal are the customer-facing prices. Omitted from list responses.

isPractice.description: Read-only. Present on GET /bids/{id}. True for the onboarding practice bid a user sends to themselves; it becomes a normal bid (false) once it is sent to anyone outside the organization.

includeNotary.description: Print the notary acknowledgment block on the pay application PDF. Defaults to true.

costPrice.description: Unit cost in dollars. For a kit (isKit: true) this is calculated from its components and read-only: a value sent on create or update is ignored.

sellPrice.description: Unit sell price in dollars. For a kit (isKit: true) this is calculated from its components and read-only: a value sent on create or update is ignored.

id.description: Id of the matched record; fetch it from that type's own endpoint.

subtitle.description: Short secondary text — email, project number, or the start of the matched body. Null when there is none.

projectId.description: Parent project for change orders, pay apps, site logs and invoices; null when the record has none. Absent for other types.

keyId.description: API key id when the caller is an API key. Null for an OAuth access token.

keyName.description: API key name when the caller is an API key. Null for an OAuth access token.

apiKey.description: Per-API-key request limit (sliding minute window). Null when the caller is OAuth/refresh-token authenticated (not an API key).

dismissedUntil.description: Snooze end, or null until the row's state changes.

token.description: The token to revoke. Can be either an access token (prefix bwp_at_) or a refresh token (prefix bwp_rt_).

token_type_hint.description: Optional hint about the token type. The server still falls back to the other type if the hinted lookup misses (RFC 7009 §4.1.2).

client_id.description: OAuth client identifier issued by the registration endpoint.

client_secret.description: Required for confidential clients; MUST be omitted for public clients.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Idempotent retry key for mutating operations. The first request with a given key executes normally and BuildWorkPro caches the response. Replaying the same key with the same request body (method + path + JSON body, SHA-256 hashed) returns the cached response without re-executing the mutation. Replaying with a DIFFERENT body returns `409 idempotency_key_reused`. The cache TTL is 24 hours; after expiry the key is treated as a new operation. Keys are tenant-scoped. Recommended: a fresh UUID v4 per logical operation.

post.summary: Move a invoice to another project
post.description: Re-points the invoice at `targetProjectId`, which must belong to your organization and must not be deleted. Needs `projects:reassign` rather than this resource's own write scope. QuickBooks is deliberately NOT rewritten: the QBO invoice keeps the customer it was pushed with, so BuildWorkPro and QuickBooks disagree about the owning job until someone reconciles them by hand. The invoice's `qboId` is left intact, and any payment-term installment link is cleared.

get.summary: Count the records still attached to a project
get.description: What a sweep would touch, broken down by record type, with the total invoiced value. Answers with an empty summary rather than 404 when nothing is attached. Needs only `projects:read`: this is the count that warns a caller before deleting a project, and deleting does not require the reassignment scope.
The ordinary project endpoints hide deleted rows. This one returns a deleted project read-only, so records stranded on it can be identified before they are moved.

post.summary: Move every record off a project
post.description: Sweeps all reassignable records from this project onto `targetProjectId` in one operation — the tool for a project deleted by mistake. `dropped` counts records the policy could not carry across (pay apps stay put: their certificates are a cumulative per-project chain). QuickBooks is never rewritten.

post.summary: Send a bid to the customer
post.description: Emails a draft bid to the customer with the PDF attached, then marks it sent. `to` and `cc` are optional; when `to` is omitted the bid's contact email is used. If there is no recipient, the bid is left unchanged. A `validUntil` already in the past is moved to today plus the organization's default bid validity, so the bid is not re-expired the night it is sent. E-signature is not available on this endpoint. A soft-deleted bid is not found.

post.description: Returns a `/b/:token` URL the customer can open without an account. Reuses a live link unless `rotate` is true. Draft and cancelled bids are refused — send the bid first. A soft-deleted bid is not found.

post.summary: Link or unlink what an invoice bills
post.description: Attach an existing invoice to the pay application, payment-schedule installment and/or bid it bills, or detach it (send `null`). Allowed in every status except `voided`, so an imported, manual or already-paid invoice can be linked after the fact; only the link columns and the derived `sourceType` change — never lines, totals or status — and nothing is pushed to QuickBooks. The pay app must be on the invoice's own project, live (submitted, sent, approved or paid) and not already claimed by another live invoice; the installment must be on the project's bid's payment term and not billed by another live invoice. An invoice bills a pay app or an installment, not both. The response carries the project's billed figures before and after; `dryRun: true` returns them without saving.

sourcePayAppId.description: Pay application this invoice bills (same project, submitted/sent/approved/paid, not claimed by another live invoice). null unlinks.

paymentTermInstallmentId.description: Payment-schedule installment this invoice bills (on the project's bid's payment term, not billed by another live invoice). null unlinks.

sourceBidId.description: The project's bid, printed on the invoice PDF. null unlinks.

dryRun.description: Validate and return the billed-figure preview without saving.

Renders an HTML consent screen. The user must be authenticated via the first-party session cookie. On approval the user is redirected to redirect_uri with `?code=&state=`. On error in the validation phase, fatal errors render an HTML error page (no redirect); validation errors after redirect_uri verification redirect with `?error=&state=`.

302.description: Redirect to client redirect_uri with code or error

post.description: Receives the user's Approve/Deny decision from the consent form. Body is form-encoded with `request_uri` (the original GET URL) and `decision` (approve or deny). Always redirects back to the client's redirect_uri.

Exchanges an authorization code (with PKCE verifier) or a refresh token for a new access token (and rotated refresh token). Body MUST be application/x-www-form-urlencoded per RFC 6749. Response carries Cache-Control: no-store. Confidential clients authenticate by passing client_secret in the body; public clients omit it. Refresh token reuse triggers family-wide revocation of all access + refresh tokens issued from the original grant.

400.description: RFC 6749 §5.2 error envelope (invalid_request, invalid_grant, invalid_client, unsupported_grant_type)

post.description: Revokes an access token or refresh token. Body MUST be application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Per RFC 7009 §2.2, the response is 200 OK whether the token was successfully revoked, already revoked, expired, or unknown — this prevents leaking information about token validity. Revoking a refresh token cascades to the entire token family (all access + refresh tokens issued from the same grant). Revoking an access token does NOT cascade.

200.description: Token revoked, already revoked, expired, or unknown — all return 200 per RFC 7009 §2.2

get.description: Returns identity information about the resource owner authenticated by the presented access token. Authentication is the standard `Authorization: Bearer` header — both API keys (bwp_live_/bwp_test_) and OAuth access tokens (bwp_at_) are accepted. No scope is required to call this endpoint.

200.description: Identity claims for the resource owner

401.description: Authentication missing, invalid, expired, or membership revoked

post.description: Self-registers a new OAuth client. Public endpoint — no authentication required. Per-IP rate-limited to 5 requests/minute. Each redirect_uri must be https, a loopback http URL on any port (http://127.0.0.1:{port}, http://localhost:{port}, http://[::1]:{port} — RFC 8252 §7.3), or a private-use scheme such as cursor:// (RFC 8252 §7.1); script-injection schemes (javascript:, data:, file:, blob:), embedded credentials, and fragments are rejected.
